To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the consumption decreases with the increase in the risk of labor income when the labor income is multiperiod and the utility function belongs to the set F.
the effect of increased risk in the multiperiod model is the same as in the single-period case for utility functions that are not concave, and that it is different for concave utility functions.
for any utility function in F, consumption increases with labor income when the income process is deterministic, and decreases when the income process becomes stochastic.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of increased uncertainty in a labor income on the optimal consumption of the consumer.
the effect of increased uncertainty in the multiperiod, optimal consumption model.
the multiperiod consumption problem with labor income.

, for utility functions belonging F and a riskless investment, the optimal consumption decreases when we move from a sequence of distribution functions to a more risky one, i.e., to a distribution function with a larger standard deviation.

, in the multiperiod, additive, utility, optimal consumption case, with a riskless asset and a stochastic labor-income, the effect of increased uncertainty on consumption is unambiguously negative.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the multiperiod case is not more complicated than the one-period case.
the effect of increased risk in labor income is a decrease in consumption.
the effect of increasing uncertainty in labor income is always to decrease consumption.
The main takeaway from our work is that
in the multiperiod model, the effect of an increase in uncertainty on optimal consumption is the same as that in the one-period model.
the optimal consumption decreases when the riskiness of the labor income increases.
the optimal consumption decreases when we move from a more certain labor income to a less certain labor income.
